#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Deploy the public demo to Cloud Run: bash scripts/deploy_cloudrun.sh <gcp-project> [region]
# One instance (min=max=1): the case cache in pawse/state.py is in memory.
# Before the first run, put the keys in Secret Manager, for example:
#   printf %s "$KEY" | gcloud secrets create pawse-gemini-key --data-file=- --project <gcp-project>
set -euo pipefail
PROJECT="${1:?usage: deploy_cloudrun.sh <gcp-project> [region]}"
REGION="${2:-europe-west6}"
SECRETS="GEMINI_API_KEY=pawse-gemini-key:latest"
if gcloud secrets describe pawse-gradium-key --project "$PROJECT" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  SECRETS="$SECRETS,REDACTED:latest"
fi
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
deploy() {
  gcloud run deploy pawse --project "$PROJECT" --region "$REGION" --source . \
    --allow-unauthenticated --min-instances 1 --max-instances 1 --timeout 3600 \
    --set-secrets "$SECRETS" --set-env-vars "^@^PAWSE_PUBLIC_DEMO=1@PAWSE_ALLOWED_HOSTS=$1" "${@:2}"
}
# The host allowlist needs the service URL, which only exists after the first deploy.
URL=$(gcloud run services describe pawse --project "$PROJECT" --region "$REGION" --format 'value(status.url)' 2>/dev/null || true)
deploy "${URL#https://}" --quiet
URL=$(gcloud run services describe pawse --project "$PROJECT" --region "$REGION" --format 'value(status.url)')
# Cloud Run serves two URLs (hash and project-number form); allow both.
HOSTS=$(gcloud run services describe pawse --project "$PROJECT" --region "$REGION" --format json | python3 -c '
import json, sys
d = json.load(sys.stdin)
urls = [d["status"]["url"], *json.loads(d["metadata"].get("annotations", {}).get("run.googleapis.com/urls", "[]"))]
print(",".join(sorted({u.removeprefix("https://") for u in urls})))')
gcloud run services update pawse --project "$PROJECT" --region "$REGION" --update-env-vars "^@^PAWSE_ALLOWED_HOSTS=$HOSTS" --quiet
curl -fsS "$URL/api/v1/health" && echo && echo "Live: $URL"

- **https://pawse-114215092948.europe-west6.run.app** is the newer, predictable format: service name, project number, region. You can work it out without deploying, and it stays the same if the service is recreated. **Use this one.**

The deploy script allows both addresses, so either one works.

# Demo check

The demo story in [research/pet-insurance/demo-video-script.md](../../../research/pet-insurance/demo-video-script.md)
is the acceptance test.

## 1. Automated first

```bash
bash scripts/check.sh                                   # safety, skills, JS syntax, OpenAPI, pytest
uvicorn pawse.app:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8765      # in a second terminal
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8765/docs >/dev/null && echo up
```

The rehearsal and demo-policy search work without provider keys. Story logic belongs in pytest
(`tests/test_orchestration.py`): assert visible outcomes (costs, citations, statuses), not internals.

## 2. Browser walkthrough

Open http://127.0.0.1:8765 and click through every scene of the story. With browser automation
(Playwright or the Chrome extension), capture a screenshot per scene and collect console errors:

```js
page.on("console", (m) => m.type() === "error" && errors.push(m.text()));
```

Look at every screenshot: overflow, cut-off text, mobile/narrow width, loading and error states,
"simulated" labels visible on every fake step. Keep screenshots out of git unless they go in the README.

## 3. Real providers

With keys in `.env`: run the care flow once with real Gemini, a voice preview with Gradium (owner
consent), and `python scripts/probe_models.py` for model access. Record results in
[docs/VALIDATION.md](../../../docs/VALIDATION.md); do not claim anything that did not run.

## 4. Demo-day checklist

- [ ] Story passes 3 times in a row on the demo machine (LLMs are flaky: tighten prompts or fake the step)
- [ ] Works on venue Wi-Fi / phone hotspot; rehearsal mode as last resort
- [ ] Microphone permission granted in the demo browser; backup video exists ([pitch](../pitch/SKILL.md))
- [ ] Zoom, notifications off, tabs pre-opened, demo state reset

## Keep this skill current

Keep commands in sync with the README quick start. Run `python scripts/validate_skills.py` after editing.
# Browser and real-speech tests (issue #25)

Automated versions of the manual checks in [docs/VALIDATION.md](../../docs/VALIDATION.md): microphone capture,
audio upload, desktop layout, the Gemini Live voice client, and recognition of English, Chinese, German and Hindi
speech. They drive the shipped pages: the React app at `/app` (built from `web/`) and the original page at `/`.

## Run

```bash
pip install -r requirements-e2e.txt && python -m playwright install chromium
PAWSE_E2E=1 python -m pytest tests/e2e                      # 62 browser tests, no keys, about 75 s
PAWSE_E2E=1 python -m pytest tests/e2e -k live_voice --headed   # watch one file
```

The suite (re)builds `web/dist` whenever it is missing or older than a `web/` source (needs Node), so it always
tests your current frontend. `bash scripts/check.sh` skips the browser tests and runs only the speech-metric tests.
Layout screenshots land in `test-results/layout/` (git-ignored) for a human look.

## What runs, and how without hardware or keys

| File | Page | What it proves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test_browser_live_voice.py` | `/app/?live=1` | Consent before any token; ephemeral token on the constrained socket; mic off until the owner turns it on; audible 16 kHz PCM at real-time pace; mute sends `audioStreamEnd` and stops audio; transcripts as text (no HTML); model audio plays and an interruption flushes it; typed text goes over the socket; tool calls forwarded once, answered and rendered; `open_clinic_call` only offers the dialer; token failure, denied mic and dropped socket are explained; hang-up and drops release the mic |
| `test_browser_recording.py` | `/app/?live=1&voice=rest`, own voice | REST fallback: one audible mono 16 kHz WAV per spoken turn, accepted by the server's validator, in the chosen language; own-voice recorder plays back locally, uploads nothing, rejects under 10 s; denied mic explained |
| `test_browser_upload.py` | `/` | Audio upload (the React app has none): 48 kHz stereo, 44.1 kHz and 8 kHz WAVs play locally and are sent as mono 16-bit; too short, too long and non-audio files are explained and never sent; a new upload replaces the old; a recorded message is audible |
| `test_browser_layout.py` | `/app`, call screen, `/` | At 1280, 1440, 1920 and 390 px: no sideways scroll, no overlapping controls, WCAG 2.2 target size (with its spacing and inline-link exceptions), call controls on screen, app column centred on desktop, demo badge visible |

- **Microphone:** Chromium's fake capture device loops 2.5 s of speech-like sound and 2.5 s of silence, so a
  silent or broken capture path fails and voice-activity detection sees turns end.
- **Gemini Live:** the Live WebSocket is answered by `FakeLive` (`e2e_helpers.py`) in the real `@google/genai`
  wire format; `/live/tokens` and `/live/tool-calls` are mocked. The app's bundled SDK, AudioWorklet and playback
  run for real.
- **Server:** the real app runs with all provider keys blanked; tests mock only the provider-backed routes they need.
- Every browser test also fails on an unexpected console error.

```bash
set -a; . ./.env; set +a     # GEMINI_API_KEY
export PAWSE_LIVE_SPEECH=1 PAWSE_RECORDINGS_DIR=/mnt/pawse-recordings
python -m pytest tests/e2e/test_real_recordings_api.py         # /voice/transcriptions (REST fallback path)

```


Everything works on the deployed version, with no console errors on any page I tested. I found four things worth fixing, mainly how the results are labelled and displayed.

**What I tested** (https://pawse-114215092948.europe-west6.run.app):

| Area | Result |
|---|---|
| API: health, capabilities, Mimi rehearsal, policy, policy search, voice status | ✅ all 200 |
| Real Gemini: care request, agent run, German vet script, live token | ✅ guidance comes back as "contact vet" in 4 to 7 s; real Zurich clinics with phone numbers from Gemini + Google Maps; German script is clean |
| AI consent off | ✅ falls back to safe generic guidance and flags `ai_consent_required` |
| `/` Mimi story, all 6 scenes with the choices clicked | ✅ every scene is labelled "Simulated"; CHF 385 vs 510 and the policy references are correct |
| `/` live care form and German script, in the browser | ✅ |
| `/app/` scripted demo | ✅ call Pawse → limping → jumped → 🟡 see a vet today → pick clinic → simulated German vet call → 16:30 → summary |
| `/app/?live=1` Gemini Live | ✅ consent screen → token → Live socket → Pawse greets. A typed message triggered the backend tool, then "Contact a vet today" and a list of real clinics. "Prepare vet conversation" opens the draft screen with "No call placed" and a dial button. |
| Phone width (390 px) | ✅ no sideways scrolling on either page |

**Issues:**
- ⚠️ **Rule 3 (honesty):** at the end of the `/app/` scripted demo, the plan card says **"✓ Booked 16:30 · ≈ CHF 600"** with no "simulated" label. The call screen itself is labelled correctly.
- ⚠️ **Live clinic list in `/app/`:** the header says "Sorted by distance", but every distance shows "–" because Gemini Maps returns no coordinates. Each card also shows a raw timestamp like `2026-10-10T14:46:16.141784+00:00`, and says "Hours unknown" even when opening hours are listed. On `/`, the first clinic was in Kilchberg rather than one near the city centre.
- ⚠️ **Live advice card in `/app/`:** the "Right now" section lists questions for the vet and services to ask about, not what to do right now. The scripted demo shows the right kind of advice there.
- ⚠️ **Location with AI consent off:** if the owner gives location consent but turns AI consent off, the coordinates still go to Gemini for the clinic search. The code does this on purpose and sends only coordinates, but the location consent text may need to say that Google gets them.

**Not tested:** cloning the owner's own voice and Gradium audio (needs a real recording and spends credits), speech recognition with a real voice (the test browser's microphone only plays a test sound), photo upload, and the insurer call in the `/app/` scripted demo.

Screenshots are in `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-azureuser-pawse/abbd5329-e9b7-4793-9b17-11b65fb12ad2/scratchpad/shots/`.

The good search is on main and on the live site, and the bad one now fails tests if anyone brings it back.

**On main** (now at `98a284f`): clinic search uses Places Text Search ("Tierarztpraxis Kleintierpraxis Tierklinik", strict vet type filtering, ranked by distance). Two filters sit on top of it:
- Eric/#70, merged after my change: drops listings that aren't open businesses or have no opening hours and fewer than 5 reviews.
- This change, #79: drops anything whose primary type isn't a vet, plus horse and farm-animal clinics.

**How the bad search is kept out:**
- **Unit tests** (they run in `bash scripts/check.sh`) check that the request is Text Search with strict filtering. They also feed in the real junk names from Zurich (psychologist, skin clinic, bird charity, a human doctor, the horse and farm-animal clinics) and check they get dropped.
- **Live test:** `tests/test_places_live.py` calls the real Places API at Zurich HB and Seefeld. It checks for at least 8 results, none of the known non-vets, and distances within 10 km. It only runs with `PAWSE_LIVE_PLACES=1` and the key, and passes today.
- **Revert check:** I temporarily switched the code back to Nearby Search. Both the unit tests and the live test failed, then I restored it.
- I also saved a note in the repo's Brain memory so other agents know not to switch back.

**Live check** after redeploying: 20 clinics near Zurich HB, all from Places and all real vet practices (Tierspital, VET Zentrum Letzigrund, Oberstrass 0.9 km, …). None of the known non-vets showed up. The deploy found all three keys already up to date.

PR: https://github.com/yyyuanfish/pawse/pull/79

⚠️ Open clinics are still listed before nearer closed ones, so Oberstrass at 0.9 km comes 4th. That's deliberate in the ranking, but the "Sorted by distance" header in `/app/` doesn't match it.
